title: HydroFusion‐GRU: A Hydrological Feedback‐Guided Deep Learning Framework for Short‐Term Daily Streamflow Forecasting
content:
ABSTRACT

Reliable short-term streamflow forecasting is essential for flood-risk assessment and water-resources management. This study proposes HydroFusion-GRU, a hydrologically guided deep learning framework for daily discharge forecasting in the 4105.2 km2 modeled catchment of the Batman River Basin, Türkiye. Using daily hydro-meteorological data from 1981 to 2023, the model combines discharge memory, meteorological forcing, temporal attention, log-residual learning, hydrological feedback, low-flow protection, and spring-runoff descriptors. The data were split chronologically into training (1981–2017), validation (2018–2021), and independent test (2022–2023) periods, with forecasts evaluated at t + 1, t + 3, and t + 7 horizons. At t + 1, HydroFusion-GRU achieved MAE = 11.698 m3/s, RMSE = 32.279 m3/s, R 2 = 0.901, and KGE = 0.950, outperforming the best conventional benchmark, HistGradientBoosting (RMSE = 35.004 m3/s; R 2 = 0.889). At t + 7, HydroFusion-GRU achieved RMSE = 52.699 m3/s and R 2 = 0.795, compared with 75.080 m3/s and 0.752 for HistGradientBoosting. Ablation analysis showed the greatest deterioration after wind removal and the smallest after precipitation removal.
